# Saved-project compatibility fixtures

`w4.openreel.json`, `w5.openreel.json`, `w6.openreel.json` and `w8.openreel.json` are project files
exactly as the w4 (`feat/premiere-parity-w4`), w5 (`feat/premiere-parity-w5`), w6
(`feat/premiere-parity-w6`) and w8 (`w8/essential-graphics`) trees write them. They are checked by `apps/web/src/test/project-compat.test.ts`:

- the file validates and imports, with the same timeline, media, text clip and marker;
- a re-save loses or changes nothing the file had (the only additions are the documented
  normalizations: the implicit main sequence for pre-w6 files, placeholder flags for media without
  a blob, default rack parameters, `generatedShaders: []`), and a second re-save is identical;
- the project opens in the project store and an edit is exactly one undo step.

What each fixture exercises: a 3-scene video track with a crossfade, an effect and a transform,
a faded audio clip on a track with an audio rack, a text clip and a marker (w4+); bins, smart bins,
media label/scene/shot/take/good-take, clip labels and a sync-lock-off track (w5+); a nest of two
clips plus a second sequence (w6); the w6 content plus an Essential Graphics lower third with edited
controls, i.e. `graphicInstances` and its member text/shape clips (w8). Older fixtures must load with no
`graphicInstances` and gain none on re-save.

## `w8-audio-repair.openreel.json`

Wave 8 audio repair (DeHum, DeClick, DeClip, DeEss, DeReverb, Gate) adds new effect types to clip
audio effects and to track / bus / master racks. It changes no required field, so the older files
above must still open untouched (checked: re-saving w4/w5/w6 never emits a repair effect) and this
file, which uses all six effect types in a clip, a track rack, a bus rack and the master rack, must
round-trip with every parameter. It is checked by `apps/web/src/test/project-compat.audio-repair.test.ts`.
It is written by the w8 tree from the w6 fixture:

```bash
cd apps/web && OPENREEL_AUDIO_REPAIR_FIXTURE_OUT=$PWD/src/test/fixtures/compat/w8-audio-repair.openreel.json \
  npx vitest run src/test/project-compat.audio-repair.test.ts -t "writes the fixture"
```

## `w9-desktop-ingest.openreel.json`

Wave 9 desktop ingest adds only optional fields: `mediaLibrary.desktopIngest` (proxy format, Proxies /
Media folders, jobs at once, proxies-with-copy), `sourceFile.path` (the file's absolute path on disk),
`copiedFrom` (copy-to-project provenance: original path + SHA-256) and, on a proxy reference, `profile`
and `previewPath` (the H.264 twin of a ProRes proxy). The older files above must still open untouched
(checked: re-saving w4..w8 never emits any of them) and this file, which uses all of them, must round-trip
with every field. It is checked by `apps/web/src/test/project-compat.desktop-ingest.test.ts` and written by
the w9 tree from the w6 fixture:

```bash
cd apps/web && OPENREEL_DESKTOP_INGEST_FIXTURE_OUT=$PWD/src/test/fixtures/compat/w9-desktop-ingest.openreel.json \
  npx vitest run src/test/project-compat.desktop-ingest.test.ts -t "writes the fixture"
```

## `w12-lumetri.openreel.json`

Wave 12 Basic Correction adds only optional fields: `clip.colorGrading.tone` (exposure, contrast, highlights,
shadows, whites, blacks), `clip.colorGrading.vignette` (amount, midpoint, roundness, feather) and keyframes on
`colorGrade.tone.*` / `colorGrade.vignette.*`. The older files above must still open untouched (checked: re-saving
w4..w9 never emits any of them) and this file, which uses all of them on one clip, must round-trip. It is checked by
`apps/web/src/test/project-compat.lumetri.test.ts` and written by the w12 tree from the w9 fixture:

```bash
cd apps/web && OPENREEL_LUMETRI_FIXTURE_OUT=$PWD/src/test/fixtures/compat/w12-lumetri.openreel.json \
  npx vitest run src/test/project-compat.lumetri.test.ts -t "writes the fixture"
```

## Regenerating

The fixtures are *generated by the tree they represent*, never hand-edited, so the bytes are what
that tree writes:

```bash
git worktree add --detach /tmp/wt-w5 feat/premiere-parity-w5
cd /tmp/wt-w5 && pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --offline
sed 's#"../src/#"./#' <repo>/apps/web/scripts/generate-compat-fixture.gen.ts > apps/web/src/gen-compat.test.ts
cd apps/web && OPENREEL_COMPAT_WAVE=w5 OPENREEL_COMPAT_OUT=<repo>/apps/web/src/test/fixtures/compat/w5.openreel.json \
  npx vitest run src/gen-compat.test.ts
cd <repo> && git worktree remove --force /tmp/wt-w5
```

Use `OPENREEL_COMPAT_WAVE=w4|w5|w6`. When a later wave changes the on-disk format, add a `w7`
fixture the same way and keep the old ones: they are the proof that old files still open.
